modern_restatement_en: Given conics $A$ and $B$, determine all (point? projective? contact?) transformations $T$ of the plane with $T(A)=B$ such that for every $P\in A$ the image of the normal to $A$ at $P$ is the normal to $B$ at $T(P)$. Do the same for quadric surfaces.
well_posed_note: The class of admissible transformations is not specified: point maps sending lines to lines, arbitrary diffeomorphisms, or contact transformations. Nor is it specified whether 'normals remain normals' means the image line, or the image curve, is the normal at the image point. Under similarities the answer is trivial (only possible if $A$ and $B$ are similar). Projective maps do not preserve normality in general, so the intended scope is unclear.

elementary_check.plan: Only after fixing a class. For instance, one could parametrise projective maps $T$ with $T(A)=B$ and require normal lines to map to normal lines on a sample of points, then solve for the parameters with sympy. That would test the conjecture that only similarities qualify within the projective group.

stackexchange: transformation mapping conic to conic preserving normal lines

belief.note: The question is too vague as posed. Natural readings either give similarities only (point-collineations), or lead to Laguerre/Lie contact geometry, which came after 1860. No known published solution.
